Question Choices: Select the correct answer. A quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides. The two non-parallel sides are equal in length. What is the most specific name? ~~Rectangle | Rhombus | Trapezoid | Isosceles-trapezoid~~
Solution: Exactly one parallel pair gives a trapezoid. Its two nonparallel sides, called legs, are equal, so the most specific name is isosceles trapezoid.

Question Choices: Select the correct answer. A quadrilateral is a rectangle, but not a square. What must be true about its sides? ~~all-sides-equal | adjacent-sides-unequal | opposite-sides-unequal~~
Hints: Check the number of parallel pairs, right angles and equal sides. A shape may belong to several families.
Solution: A rectangle has equal opposite sides. If adjacent sides were equal too, all four sides would match and it would be a square. Since it is not a square, adjacent sides are unequal.

Question Choices: Select True or False of the statement "Rectangle meets the rules for both parallelogram and quadrilateral" ~~TRUE | FALSE~~
Hints: Check the number of parallel pairs, right angles and equal sides. A shape may belong to several families.
Solution: A rectangle has four sides, making it a quadrilateral, and two parallel opposite-side pairs, making it a parallelogram. TRUE.

Question Choices: Select which of the following shapes are always rectangles? ~~Square | Rhombus | Parallelogram~~
Hints: Check the number of parallel pairs, right angles and equal sides. A shape may belong to several families.
Solution: A square always has four right angles, so it is a rectangle. General rhombuses and parallelograms may have non-right angles.

Question Choices: A farmer encloses a property with four fences. The north and south fences run completely parallel to each other, but the east and west fences are completely non-parallel and unequal in length. What is the most specific geometric name for this plot of land? : Parallelogram Rhombus Trapezoid
Hints: Count parallel side pairs, then compare the two nonparallel sides. Equal legs give an isosceles trapezoid.
Solution: Exactly one parallel pair makes this a trapezoid. A parallelogram, rectangle or rhombus has two parallel pairs. The unequal legs rule out an isosceles trapezoid.
